faults.where: screen target chip and readout vs spec items
faults.detail: Spec items are "target": 6, "show": "cm" on a ruler with "scaleMax": 10, but both screens show the target as "0.6 cm" and the readout "0.6 cm". The graded value on screen disagrees with the spec value 6 cm.

faults.where: ruler labels at p412 and l1366
faults.detail: The ruler is labelled "0", "1" (at the middle) and "1" (at the end). A 10-tick ruler with scaleMax 10 should read 0, 5, 10 (or 0 to 10); the middle "1" and end "1" are wrong numbers for the marks drawn, and contradict a 0.6 cm target sitting near the first tick.

faults.where: rounds[0]: "Marks ko dekho" / "Dono marks ko gaur se dekho", items target 6 and 6
faults.detail: The mix-up is starting from the ruler edge or from 1 instead of 0, or reading only the end number. The bar starts at 0 and both items are the same plain target 6; nothing places an object starting off 0 (e.g. 3 to 9), so a child holding the belief would not go wrong here.

faults.where: rounds[0].sub: "Dono marks ko gaur se dekho"
faults.detail: The sub-title speaks of "dono marks" (two marks) but the screen shows no two distinguished marks (start and end) to compare; words disagree with the picture.

faults.where: ruler end label at p412 and l1366
faults.detail: The end label reads "1" at the right edge, apparently a clipped "10"; the label is cut off at both sizes.

Title says "1 km ka case" but every item is a capacity in millilitres ("target": 1000, "show": "ml"; screen shows "1000 ml" and a jug scaled "4000 ml"). The words disagree with the round: there is no km or m anywhere on the board.

The topic is length conversion (km to m; cards: "How many metres make 1 km?", "Write 3 km in metres.", "2 km 50 m = ___ m"). The piece practises pouring 1000 ml, 3000 ml, 2050 ml into a measuring jug, which is capacity, not length.

The mix-up is "Believes 1 km = 100 m". The child is only asked to pour a stated amount ("1000 ml") to the matching jug mark; no km is ever converted, so a child holding the 1 km = 100 m belief would pour correctly and the belief would never show.

faults.where: screen target chip "1000 ml" and jug label "1000"
faults.detail: The value to place is stated as "1000 ml" and the jug has a labelled "1000" mark, so the task is just matching the same number; the conversion the round's title ("1 km ka case") implies is stated rather than asked.

The only task is to pour 36 ml into a 0-100 ml container (screen: "36 ml"). No decimal (e.g. 0.36) and no fraction (36/100) appears anywhere, so a child who believes 0.5 = 1/5 or 0.36 is 'a separate whole number 36' never meets the point where that belief goes wrong. Pouring a whole number of ml does not test the decimal-fraction link.

faults.where: spec.title "Dashamlav ko jodo"; rounds[0].title "Hisson ka naap"
faults.detail: The topic is decimals as tenths/hundredths linked to fractions (cards: 0.1 m, 7/10 = 0.7, 0.36 = 36/100). The piece practises reading a whole-number ml scale, which is not this topic's idea.

faults.where: spec.title "Dashamlav ko jodo" vs rounds[0] items "36 ml"
faults.detail: The title says 'connect the decimals' but the round contains no decimal at all; the words disagree with the round's own content.

faults.where: rounds[0].sub "Har case ko dhyan se dekho"
faults.detail: The sub-title refers to every case ('har case') but the round has a single item (36 ml); the words disagree with their own round.

notes: The large box showing "36 ml" on the first screen with an empty container is presumably the target readout, not a live reading; from the packet I cannot tell whether it updates while pouring, so not counted.
